title: Fix scheduler starvation & tail-latency for long-context continuous batching
creator: Kayla Morgan
description:
Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported intermittent high tail latency and request starvation on endpoints using continuous batching with long-context models. The issue surfaces as: some requests (typically long-context or low-frequency tenants) are delayed by several hundred milliseconds to multiple seconds, while overall throughput appears normal. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations, and the long-term fix to the scheduler and batching heuristics.

Observed symptoms:
- Tail-latency spikes concentrated on requests with >8k tokens (long-context) and requests that append new tokens to an existing KV cache.
- Queue starvation: small, low-rate tenants observed to wait behind large bursty tenants for extended periods.
- Dedicated nodes under memory pressure show increased scheduling jitter leading to batch formation timeouts.
- Private customer (on-prem) reported cascading timeouts due to aggressive backoff in our per-tenant fair-queue reconciler.

Impact: High (customer-facing incidents: Acme Health, FinEdge). Incidents caused degraded SLAs for multi-tenant hosted customers and two Dedicated customers had pages.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use load generator to send mixed workload: 60% short requests (<512 tokens) at high QPS, 40% long requests (~12k token seq) at low QPS across 50 tenants.
2) Enable continuous batching runtime with default scheduler config (batch_window=10ms, max_batch_size=64, per_tenant_weighting=false).
3) Observe per-tenant queue lengths and scheduler logs: starvation appears when a burst of short requests continually forms full batches, preventing scheduler from aging in long requests.
4) Reproduce on Dedicated pool with simulated memory pressure (reducing KV cache capacity) to trigger additional batch formation delays.

Test harness: scripts/perf/continuous_batching/starvation_test.py and load profiles in perf/fixtures/long_context.json
root_cause:
Three contributing issues found: 1) Scheduling fairness bug: the batcher used a simple greedy fill strategy without an effective aging mechanism; long-context requests stayed at the head of queue until a full batch formed which rarely happens under bursty short-request traffic, causing starvation. 2) Batch-window tuning: the 10ms window plus high throughput of short requests produced many full batches and prevented the scheduler from opening a sub-window to capture aged long-context items. 3) KV-cache interaction: long-context requests often miss cached prefixes on Dedicated/Private nodes during memory pressure, increasing per-request latency and making them less likely to be coalesced into timely batches.

Combined, these made long-context tails both slower and less likely to be prioritized, amplifying customer impact.
mitigation:
Immediate hotfix (deployed 2026-03-03):
- Introduced aging counter on queue entries (age-based priority boost after 25ms).
- Cap per-tenant contribution to a batch to 40% so a single tenant cannot monopolize batch slots.
- Lowered default batch_window to 6ms for hosted tier and made it adaptive based on observed sequence-length mix.
- Added memory pressure signal to reduce batch size proactively on affected Dedicated nodes.

These changes were rolled as a canary to 5% of Hosted traffic and two Dedicated pools for 6 hours, validated using latency histograms and tenant fairness metrics. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/9812
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (Canary): 5% Hosted + two Dedicated pools, 6 hours monitoring for regressions. Metrics: p50/p95/p99 by seq-length, per-tenant wait-time, batch fill rates.
Phase 2 (Ramp): 25% -> 50% over 24 hours if stable.
Phase 3 (Global): 100% with rolling restarts limited per-region.
Private customers: packaging as runtime-1.20-rc2; owners notified for in-place upgrade. For air-gapped installs we provide patch bundle and upgrade notes.
Rollback criteria: p99 latency increase >10% for short-context requests or error rate rise >0.5% over baseline.
tests_and_validation:
Automated: added unit tests for aging priority and per-tenant caps; integration tests simulate mixed seq-length traffic.
Perf: stress tests run in the perf cluster with 24-hour run comparing before/after p99 tail latency for long-context.
Canary dashboards: batcher_latency_by_seq_length, tenant_wait_time_percentile, batch_fill_distribution.
Postmortem checks: ensure KV cache hit rate improves after adaptive sizing and that memory-pressure signal triggers expected behavior.
next_steps:
1) Merge scheduler hotfix into runtime-1.20 and ship runtime-1.20.0.
2) Implement improved KV-cache prefetch heuristics for long-context sessions (follow-up ticket ENG-2945).
3) Add tenant-level admission control to protect very low-frequency tenants (design doc linked).
4) Ship observability improvements: per-tenant starvation alerts and automated ticketing.
5) Coordinate communications: a short status email to affected customers with timeline and mitigations performed.
